headline: Gas shortage disrupts transport and sparks power cuts across Bangladesh
summary: Long queues at CNG stations and extensive power outages are causing widespread public suffering, with no immediate solution in sight for the ongoing energy crisis.
details: Bangladesh is currently experiencing a severe gas shortage, leading to significant disruptions in both public transport services and electricity supply nationwide. Commuters are facing immense difficulties due to long queues at CNG filling stations, impacting daily routines and economic activities.

The energy crisis has also resulted in extensive power cuts across the country. Data reveals a sharp increase in the average daily power shortfall, reaching a staggering 1,482 megawatts between July 26 and August 1, up from 320 megawatts in the preceding week.

This escalating shortage is causing widespread public suffering, with businesses and households struggling to cope with the unreliable power supply and limited transport options. Authorities are yet to announce concrete measures to alleviate the immediate crisis.

headline: LPG price hike effective from evening in Bangladesh; Jamaat expresses concern
summary: The price adjustment for Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) was announced and took effect from the evening. This development has prompted political reactions, with Jamaat-e-Islami expressing concern over the increased cost.
details: The price of Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) has been increased in Bangladesh. The new prices became effective from the evening of the announcement.
Following the announcement, Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami voiced its concern regarding the LPG price hike. The political party highlighted the potential burden on consumers.
caption:
LPG prices in Bangladesh have increased, taking effect from this evening. This adjustment is expected to impact household budgets across the country.
